method.name: NXGO architecture FMEA
method.notes: Scores are engineering prioritization aids, not a safety certification. Severity is not reduced by controls; occurrence and detection may improve as controls/evidence mature.

risks.title: Ambiguous RPC outcome and unsafe replay
risks.failure_mode: A mutating request is sent, the response path is lost or cancelled, and the caller cannot prove whether NX committed the operation.
risks.effect: Blind retry can duplicate or conflict with CAD mutations and diverge client-visible state from the NX session.
causes: request replay without durable outcome identity
controls: bounded production request journal with payload fingerprint
worker recycle on unsafe session state
next_actions: retain real-NX commit/lost-response replay evidence in release matrix
keep replay semantics identical between Fake Agent and production Agent
acceptance_criteria: no cancelled-before-start mutation executes later
same RequestID replay never duplicates a committed mutation
ambiguous outcomes force quarantine instead of transparent retry

risks.title: Stale or foreign ObjectRef targets the wrong NX object
risks.failure_mode: A stale, released, wrong-kind, cross-session or reused handle resolves to an unintended live object.
risks.effect: A syntactically valid request can mutate the wrong part, body, feature or component.
controls: no implicit work/display-part fallback for invalid explicit refs
next_actions: preserve invalid-reference real-NX fixtures for every new mutating domain
review ownership graphs when new proxy types are introduced
acceptance_criteria: invalid explicit references fail before NX mutation
closed owner invalidates descendants
slot reuse with old generation never resolves

risks.title: NX execution occurs on an unsupported thread or reentrant context
risks.failure_mode: Transport or callback code executes NXOpen outside the bound NX-safe execution context, or a callback reenters the executor unsafely.
risks.effect: Deadlock, NX instability, corrupted session state or non-reproducible behavior.
causes: direct NXOpen call from transport thread
controls: NXOpen dependency limited to NXHost boundary
next_actions: add explicit callback/reentrancy fixtures as callback-driven APIs are added
keep Siemens references statically forbidden outside NXHost
acceptance_criteria: all NX-affecting work crosses the canonical executor
executor drain on wrong thread fails closed
no release adapter duplicates execution logic

risks.title: Partial mutation, incomplete update or unsafe rollback leaves poisoned session reusable
risks.failure_mode: A builder or update fails after partial CAD state changes and cleanup/rollback does not restore a known-safe state.
risks.effect: Subsequent operations run against inconsistent geometry while the worker is still reported healthy.
next_actions: complete explicit UpdateManager/update recipe for every mutating operation
add rollback-failure and postcondition-failure state classification fixtures
require risk review for every new builder-backed API
acceptance_criteria: every mutating operation declares update and rollback policy
failed postcondition cannot leave worker Healthy without proof
rollback failure forces quarantine/recycle

risks.title: NX release/runtime load-context incompatibility
risks.failure_mode: A supported NX release loads NXOpen or the Agent through a different managed/native runtime contract than the qualified releases.
risks.effect: Agent bootstrap may fail, type identity may split, or behavior may differ despite successful compilation.
controls: no reflection crossing NXOpen load contexts
next_actions: qualify each new NX family through bootstrap before domain expansion
retain loader mode and assembly hashes in release evidence
acceptance_criteria: Session acquisition and handshake pass on every claimed release
no cross-load-context NXOpen object reflection
release claim has retained real-NX evidence

risks.title: Engineering unit or semantic drift produces plausible but wrong CAD data
risks.failure_mode: Geometry, mass, transform, angle or density values are converted with the wrong unit contract or interpreted differently across APIs/releases.
risks.effect: Automation returns numerically plausible but physically incorrect results or creates incorrect geometry.
next_actions: require unit metadata for any new ambiguous quantity
add analytical and differential oracles for new geometry domains
acceptance_criteria: metric and imperial fixtures represent the same physical result
every public dimensional field has a declared unit contract
aggregation semantics are explicit

risks.title: Generated raw API or capability map drifts from real NX surface
risks.failure_mode: Scanner/binding generation misses overload or signature changes, or advertises a capability that the release adapter cannot safely dispatch.
risks.effect: Compile-time success hides runtime dispatch failure or semantic mismatch on a supported NX release.
next_actions: complete reproducible 2512-to-2606 compatibility report
differentially compare representative scanner output with Siemens tooling where available
gate capabilities on generated dispatch plus release evidence
acceptance_criteria: binding regeneration is deterministic
overload/signature deltas are explicit
no capability is advertised without matching dispatch and release evidence

risks.title: Handle, journal, queue or process resources grow without bound
risks.failure_mode: Long-running workers accumulate handles, journal records, queued work, memory or native resources until latency or stability degrades.
risks.effect: Worker becomes slow, hits capacity, fails mid-workflow or destabilizes NX.
next_actions: keep per-domain long-lived soak when ownership changes
surface all high-watermarks in doctor/session telemetry
acceptance_criteria: defined representative soak reaches a stable plateau
capacity exhaustion fails closed
worker recycle occurs before unsafe reuse

risks.title: Local IPC endpoint can be impersonated or used by an unintended process
risks.failure_mode: Another local process connects to or impersonates the named pipe and sends valid-looking control or CAD requests.
risks.effect: Unauthorized CAD mutation, data disclosure or denial of service under the current user/session.
next_actions: complete explicit Windows per-user DACL when a supported reproducible API/package path is available
keep unauthorized-client and flooding tests in real-NX gate
acceptance_criteria: untrusted local client cannot complete authenticated handshake
endpoint is scoped to intended worker/session
ACL hardening is reproducible on supported Windows runners

risks.title: Save/export reports success before durable artifact publication
risks.failure_mode: Part save, SaveAs, PDF or export partially succeeds or writes a temporary/incomplete artifact that is reported as final.
risks.effect: User receives missing, corrupt or stale engineering output despite a successful API result.
next_actions: stage externally published files and atomically publish where the destination permits
define durability semantics per export type
acceptance_criteria: explicit save failure is observable
success implies validated intended artifact
partial publish cannot replace prior valid artifact where atomic staging is available

risks.title: Simulated evidence overstates production or release safety
risks.failure_mode: Fake Agent, unit tests or documentation prove stronger behavior than the real NX production path actually enforces.
risks.effect: Unsafe semantics are released because green fast tests are mistaken for real-NX proof.
causes: documentation status conflates E2 and E3/E4
next_actions: require explicit evidence class on major capability claims
keep Fake/production shared conformance suites for safety contracts
acceptance_criteria: documentation never claims a higher evidence class than retained evidence
production path uses tested Core primitives
compatibility claim references a successful release run

risks.title: Public API accepts parameters or abstractions the backend does not faithfully implement
risks.failure_mode: The SDK accepts a parameter or exposes a stable abstraction while the NX adapter ignores it, hardcodes different behavior or leaks raw-version-specific semantics.
risks.effect: Calls succeed syntactically but create the wrong engineering result or lock the public API to unstable NX details.
next_actions: require real-NX semantic fixture before marking new public mutating options done
keep transport DTOs and generated raw types out of domain contracts
acceptance_criteria: every accepted public parameter changes or validates the intended semantics
unsupported behavior is rejected explicitly
domain API remains independent of generated raw package shape

risks.title: Fine-grained IPC or long NX operations create timeout and recovery cascades
risks.failure_mode: N+1 calls, oversized queries or long serialized operations saturate the worker and trigger client timeouts/quarantine during otherwise valid workloads.
risks.effect: Throughput collapse, unnecessary worker recycle and increased ambiguous-outcome exposure.
next_actions: define batch/page limits for large-assembly and raw-layer operations
track RPC count and queue wait time as first-class performance metrics
acceptance_criteria: high-volume APIs are coarse/bulk by default
queue saturation fails predictably
representative workloads remain below timeout and resource thresholds

risks.title: Modal UI, journal stickiness or interactive state blocks unattended automation
risks.failure_mode: An NX operation opens modal UI, inherits sticky interactive state or requires a journal/UI condition unavailable to the worker.
risks.effect: Worker hangs indefinitely, supervisor times out, or behavior differs between interactive and unattended runs.
next_actions: classify APIs that can trigger modal interaction before admitting them to public domains
add watchdog evidence for dialog-prone operations
acceptance_criteria: unattended operation cannot wait indefinitely on modal UI
journal fallback is explicit and policy-controlled
interactive-state dependency is documented or normalized

risks.title: External side effects cannot be rolled back with the NX session
risks.failure_mode: A workflow mutates NX and also publishes files or updates an external system such as Designcenter/Teamcenter, then fails between side effects.
risks.effect: NX model, published artifacts and external metadata become inconsistent with no ACID rollback path.
controls: architecture explicitly rejects cross-system ACID assumption
next_actions: define saga/compensation contract before external-system write support
stage artifacts before publication
record durable workflow step identity and recovery state
add crash injection between every external side effect
acceptance_criteria: each external side effect has an idempotency or compensation strategy
workflow recovery can distinguish committed NX state from published external state
no external write domain ships without crash-transition tests

risks.title: Capability, license or partial-load state is mistaken for full model availability
risks.failure_mode: The SDK assumes a capability/license is available or an assembly is fully loaded when NX is in a partial/suppressed/unlicensed state.
risks.effect: Queries return incomplete engineering data or mutations fail midway with release/license-specific behavior.
causes: capability negotiation not coupled to runtime state
next_actions: treat load completeness and license state as explicit preconditions for affected operations
add partial-load and license-loss fixtures to each dependent domain
acceptance_criteria: incomplete assembly state is visible in results or rejected
license-dependent API reports stable typed failure
capability advertisement does not imply current license availability
